entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ælfthryth of Wessex, also known as Elftrudis , was an English princess and a countess consort of Flanders to Baldwin II. She was born around 920 to King Edgar of Wessex and his wife  Ethelflåd, daughter of King Alfred the Great's sister  Ealhswith. Ælfthryth married Baldwin II in 944 and became Countess of Flanders, playing a crucial role in Flanders' politics and trade. She died on June 7, 929, leaving behind a legacy as one of the most influential women in medieval Flanders.

Ælfthryth's reign was marked by significant political and economic changes in Flanders. She worked to strengthen the county's trade relationships with England and the Holy Roman Empire, and her diplomatic efforts helped to maintain peace between Flanders and neighboring territories. Ælfthryth's influence extended beyond her political role, as she patronized the arts and supported the development of Flanders' textile industry.

Ælfthryth's significance extends beyond her own time period. Her legacy as a powerful and influential woman in medieval Flanders has inspired generations of historians and scholars. Her life and reign serve as a reminder of the important role women played in shaping the course of European history.

"The Countess of Flanders will always be remembered as a shining example of a woman who broke the mold of traditional gender roles and achieved greatness through her own merits."
